title: Why Generate a Click? Plug-in Decision Heads for Web Agents
summary: The method replaces text-based action decoding (generating tokens like click(12)) with lightweight classification heads that read action type, target element, and text-option choices directly from the frozen generator's hidden states, falling back to full decoding from the same forward pass's KV cache when head confidence is low. Costs include training the heads on web-step data (the paper used 213k steps), an additional confidence-threshold hyperparameter per deployment, and up to 2 points of step-success regression on some benchmarks (GUIAct, MiniWoB++) under loose thresholds. Failures after adoption can come from miscalibrated confidence on out-of-distribution websites, from UI layouts whose element structure differs from training data, and from degradation of the generator itself if heads are trained jointly rather than on frozen weights (up to 4.9 points of generator step-success loss).
rationale: The approach fits a single-GPU budget and cuts inference cost for web-agent workloads, but it requires training task-specific heads and tuning confidence thresholds against the reader's own web environment before production adoption.
technique: Plug-in decision heads on frozen VLM web agents

Costs include training the heads on web-step data (the paper used 213k steps), an additional confidence-threshold hyperparameter per deployment, and up to 2 points of step-success regression on some benchmarks (GUIAct, MiniWoB++) under loose thresholds. WebArena task success rises from 12.5% to 13.8% (Qwen3-VL 4B) and from 13.6% to 14.6% (8B) while generating less than half the tokens; a strict threshold keeps offline step success within -0.3 to +1.4 points across seven test sets with 12-64% of steps decided by heads.
